name: Ba Be
provinceNote: National Assembly Resolution 202/2025/QH15 folded Bắc Kạn into Thái Nguyên. New provincial governments started work on 1 July 2025. The park was under the Cao Bằng People’s Committee only from 1992 to 1997.
dotReason: The lake is the reason for the night, and the park is the frame of the trip.
summary: A national park lake in the northern hills, ringed by limestone and forest, with boat trips and Tay villages. Spend a slow day on the water, sleep in a stilt house at Pac Ngoi or Bo Lu, and eat grilled lake fish and five-colour sticky rice. Two nights suits nature lovers who want quiet time away from Hanoi.
fee: Check on arrival. No park tariff is published. Operator sheets were not used as the fee. Lake: 150 m above sea level, about 178 m, and 145 m. Length 7.5 km, to 8 km, and longer than 8 km. Depth 17–23 m, 17–29 m, and average 20 m. Deepest 29 m and about 35 m. Park 10,048 ha. One split: strict protection 4,010.70 ha, ecological restoration 5,375.60 ha, admin-service 57.40 ha, inner buffer 604.0 ha, outer buffer 25,309 ha. Another split of the same 10,048 ha: 3,846 ha strict, 6,162 ha restoration, and 40 ha admin. Mountain roads in a storm: Check on arrival. Boat seat count: Check on arrival. Gate-to-house minutes: Check on arrival. Minutes from Pac Ngoi to Bo Lu: Check on arrival. A closing hour for then singing: Check on arrival. Whether the Bac Kan–Ba Be–Na Hang road or the road around the lake is open as a bus loop: Check on arrival.
getThere: Road from Hanoi. The park is 250 km northeast of Hanoi, about 240 km northeast, and 250 km north of Hanoi. It is 68 km northwest of Bac Kan city. Bac Kan city is 165 km from Hanoi, then the lake is a further leg. A single door-to-door kilometre: Check on arrival. Hanoi to Bac Kan city: about 3 hours on old National Highway 3, which motorbikes can use, or about 2 hours by the Hanoi–Thai Nguyen expressway and then National Highway 3, cars only. Those hours stop at the city, not the lake. From the city, provincial road 256 is about 60 km, or provincial road 257 via Cho Don is about 70 km. The city-to-park figure is also 68 km. Minutes on the last leg: Check on arrival. The lake is about 220 km from Noi Bai. Those minutes: Check on arrival. No airfield at the lake is named. No rail station is named. Coaches leave My Dinh in Hanoi on Hanoi–Bac Kan and Hanoi–Cao Bang lines, and those lines often pass the lake. Operator clocks and fares: Check on arrival. Cho Ra is the commune on the park’s north edge. Puong Cave is 5 km from the old town of Cho Ra. That is the cave, not a measured walk from the market to Pac Ngoi. Boats leave bến Buốc Lốm, about 1 km down the Nang to Puong. Two starts are named, the lake and the Nang, with 12 seats for a domestic group and 10 for an international group. The map point is the middle of the box 22°06'12"–22°08'14" N and 105°09'07"–105°12'22" E. The UNESCO box for the whole tentative property is a different outline. It is not a gate pin. Admin: the park was under the Cao Bằng People’s Committee only from 1992 to 1997, then the agriculture ministry until 2003, then Bắc Kạn until 1 July 2025.
seoTitle: Ba Be travel guide — the lake boat, Puong Cave, Tay stilt houses
seoDescription: Take the boat on Ba Be Lake, through Puong Cave, and sleep in a Tay stilt house at Pac Ngoi. The lake is in Thái Nguyên.
intro: You step into a boat on Ba Be Lake, green water between limestone and forest on the walls, and ride toward the Tay stilt roofs at Pac Ngoi. Sleep in a Tay house at Pac Ngoi, on the Leng where it meets the lake, or at Bo Lu, where the festival ground is, so the landing is a morning.

Stay if the lake is the trip. Go to Cao Bang if you wanted Ban Gioc and the geopark. Those are a different road. The lake is in Thái Nguyên. It is not part of Cao Bang, and it is not a day that starts and ends in Hanoi.

The mistake is budgeting Puong Cave, Dau Dang, Hua Ma Cave, and the Keo Siu walk as one hour. The cave and the fall are one boat. Hua Ma is a walk on the south side. Keo Siu to An Ma is 5–6 hours. Do not swim in Fairy Pond. That water is sacred: no hands or feet in it.
gettingAround: The usual previous stop is Hanoi. You ride to Bac Kan city, then on to the lake. No airfield at the lake is named, and no rail station is named. Coaches leave My Dinh on the Hanoi–Bac Kan and Hanoi–Cao Bang lines, and those lines often pass the lake.

Cho Ra is the commune on the park’s north edge. A last-mile motorbike runs from the park gate into the village. On the water, boats leave bến Buốc Lốm, about 1 km down the Nang to Puong. A dugout is one tree, about 50 cm wide and 5–10 m long, with one paddle, often for 2–3 people.
The district is investing in a Bac Kan–Ba Be–Na Hang road and in the road around the lake.

stayAreas.name: Pac Ngoi
stayAreas.summary: Tay stilt houses on the Leng, against the lake. Nearly 60 homestay households are counted in Nam Mau. A room that looks at the lake is one of those houses. Fuller facilities sit 1–2 km off the shore at the park gate. The hamlet has few stores, so the meal is booked with the house. No hotel brand as a pick.

stayAreas.name: Bo Lu
stayAreas.summary: The other homestay cluster, and the shore where Long Tong opens. The 2026 festival was at Bo Lu, xa Ba Be. No hotel brand as a pick.

eat: The meal is the Tay table in the stilt house at Pac Ngoi, or at Bo Lu when Long Tong is on. The table runs to grilled lake fish, sour shrimp, forest bamboo shoot, upland sticky rice, and roast suckling pig, with leaf-yeast wine when the singing is on. Also grilled shrimp, pork over the fire, and khau nhuc. Five-colour sticky rice is the festival rice. The full list is on the food guide. Book the meal and carry water. The hamlet has few shops.
interestsBody: The morning is the boat on the lake. The same circuit takes you through Puong Cave and, if it is the long one, to Dau Dang. The night is the stilt-house floor at Pac Ngoi, not a bar street.

An Ma and Widow Island are landmarks on that boat. Fairy Pond is a look, and swimming is forbidden. Hua Ma Cave is a walk on the south side. Tat Ma is a named fall in Dong Phuc. Cho Ra is the road town on the north edge.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: The Tay table in the stilt house: grilled lake fish, sour shrimp, upland sticky rice, and five-colour sticky rice.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Grilled lake fish, sour shrimp, bamboo-tube rice, and five-colour sticky rice at the house.

interestGroups.title: The lake at breakfast
interestGroups.summary: A morning on the water, with limestone on the walls and a boat at the landing.
body: Tay speakers call the widenings Slam Pe: Pe Leng, Pe Lu, and Pe Lam. The water is one lake running nearly 8 km north–south, and it is also described as three lakes joined. You ride a boat. The usual circuit is the open water, An Ma, Fairy Pond, Puong, and Dau Dang, in combinations the boatman sells.

cards.title: Ba Be Lake
cards.summary: Green water, limestone, and the boats at the landing. Come for the morning.

interestGroups.title: The river cave and the fall
interestGroups.summary: The boat that goes through Puong and lands at Dau Dang. They are one circuit.
body: Puong is on the Nang, about 1 km downstream from bến Buốc Lốm. The cave is 300 m long, with a ceiling of 30–40 m. Dau Dang is about 3 km west of the lake. The fall is about 53 m. The slope of the stacked rock is estimated at 500 m. That 500 m is the slope, not a vertical drop.

cards.title: Puong Cave
cards.summary: Sit in the boat while it goes through. Footsteps, torchlight, and talking wake the bats.

cards.title: Dau Dang
cards.summary: White water on stacked rock, about 3 km west of the lake. The fish run is March and April.

interestGroups.title: Tay houses on the Leng
interestGroups.summary: A night in a stilt house that faces the water, not a shop street.
body: Pac Ngoi is the Tay village on the Leng. Nearly 100 stilt roofs, some a century old, and about 80 percent of the old houses are still standing. About 40 nhân khẩu is a different count. Tay people are 57 percent of people living in the park, and Mong 37 percent. After the meal, then singing and the đàn tính are the evening, if the house has called the hamlet troupe.

cards.title: Pac Ngoi
cards.summary: Stilt houses, the Leng, and the cliff. Sleep here so the boat is a morning.

interestGroups.title: Limestone forest
interestGroups.summary: The karst forest around the lake, and the walk with a clock.
body: The park is 10,048 ha. One split is strict protection 4,010.70 ha, ecological restoration 5,375.60 ha, admin-service 57.40 ha, and an inner buffer of 604.0 ha, plus an outer buffer of 25,309 ha. The same 10,048 ha is also split into 3,846 ha strict, 6,162 ha restoration, and 40 ha admin. The walk with a clock is Keo Siu to An Ma, 5–6 hours, through forest called primary. It is not a gentle outing.

cards.title: Ba Be National Park
cards.summary: Karst, forest, and the lake in one frame. The park is the whole trip.

interestGroups.title: Islands in the water
interestGroups.summary: The islands you pass on the boat. They are lake islands, not a sea crossing.
body: Widow Island and An Ma sit in the water. Widow Island is in Pe Leng, stacked rock held by tree roots. No landing pier is named. An Ma rises about 30 m, in a turtle-shell curve, and the temple is a Tay and Nung worship site.

cards.title: Islands in the lake
cards.summary: An island in the water, with the cliff behind.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: OCOP counters in Chợ Rã and Nam Mẫu, and the weekend market remembered at Pac Ngoi.

blocks.heading: Cho Ra and Nam Mau
paragraphs: Two OCOP counters, one in thị trấn Chợ Rã and one in xã Nam Mẫu, sell the gifts: fragrant green squash and its tea, dried buffalo, dong vermicelli, jiaogulan tea, dried banana, kitchen-hung sausage, Nà Hai spring wine, and Nếp Tài rice. Seeded banana is sold on the path up to Ao Tiên and from the gate down to the lake.

blocks.heading: Pac Ngoi night market
paragraphs: In September 2019 a weekend night market at Pac Ngoi, over the 2 September holiday, sold bamboo-tube rice, grilled fish, five-colour sticky rice, bánh gai, and bánh dày gấc.

cards.title: OCOP counters
cards.summary: Gifts at the counters in Chợ Rã and Nam Mẫu.

cards.title: Pac Ngoi market
cards.summary: The 2019 weekend market at the stilt houses, over the 2 September holiday.

season.label: Year round
season.note: Two seasons, a northeast monsoon, a year-round mean of 22°C, about 1,378 mm of rain, and humidity above 80 percent. April–October is called the rainy season and November–February the dry season. Some places fall to 0°C with ice. February–April is the pleasant window at 25–30°C, beside the 22°C mean. March and April, after the first rains, are when fish run Dau Dang. Long Tong is the 10th of the first lunar month. The 2024 opening was 19 February and the 2026 opening was 26 February. The next civil date moves.

faqs.q: How big is Ba Be Lake?
faqs.a: Height is 150 m above sea level, about 178 m, and 145 m. Length is 7.5 km, to 8 km, and longer than 8 km. Depth is 17–23 m, 17–29 m, and an average of 20 m. The deepest point is 29 m and about 35 m.

faqs.q: Is Ba Be part of Cao Bang?
faqs.a: The lake is in Thái Nguyên after Resolution 202/2025/QH15 folded Bắc Kạn into that province. The park was under the Cao Bằng People’s Committee only from 1992 to 1997. Cao Bằng was not merged.

faqs.q: What does the park ticket cost?
faqs.a: No park tariff is published. Ask at the gate. Operator sheets were not used as the fee.
